metaDescription: Six mulching lawn mowers compared by blade design, power source, drive and deck, from cordless self-propelled to gas and corded, for finer clippings.
expertTake: The EGO LM2134SP-2 is the best mulching mower for most lawns because it includes a true mulching blade, Touch Drive and 100 minutes of runtime. The WORX WG752 is the value cordless pick, and the YARDMAX is the choice for big or hilly lawns that need gas. Skip mulching entirely if your lawn is mostly tall, wet or seeding weeds, and bag instead.
introParagraphs: A mulching mower cuts grass clippings into fine pieces and drops them back into the lawn, where they break down and feed the soil. That only works with a sealed deck, a blade built to recut clippings and enough power to keep the blade spinning through thick grass.

This guide explains how mulching blades and decks work, why mowing height and grass condition change results, and how to choose between battery, gas and corded power. The top picks are above, and the reviews below show which mower fits which lawn.

buyingCriteria.explanation: True mulching needs a blade with a curved profile and a deck that stays sealed so clippings circulate and are cut repeatedly. A mulch plug in a side-discharge deck is a compromise because the chute geometry is not designed for recutting. The EGO LM2134SP-2 ships a dedicated mulching blade as part of its Select Cut system, while the WORX WG752 and DOVAMAN use plugs. If clippings pile up in rows, the blade or the deck is the problem.

Battery mowers have no fuel or carburetor, but runtime sets the limit. The EGO LM2134SP-2 lists up to 100 minutes with two 6.0 Ah batteries, the Greenworks 60V up to three quarters of an acre, and the WORX WG752 up to half an acre. Gas mowers such as the YARDMAX 201cc and PowerSmart 144cc run as long as the tank lasts. Corded mowers like the DOVAMAN are limited by the cord.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Cutting Height and the One-Third Rule
buyingCriteria.explanation: Mulching works best when you remove no more than about a third of the grass blade, so clippings are short and settle quickly. Cutting heights vary: the EGO runs from 1 to 4 inches, the PowerSmart 1.5 to 3.9 and the DOVAMAN only 0.98 to 2.95. If your lawn gets tall between mowings, you need a wide height range and more power. Raise the deck and take two passes rather than forcing a short cut.

Self-propel reduces effort on slopes and big lawns, and mulching often requires slower walking in thick grass. The EGO, Greenworks 60V and YARDMAX are self-propelled, while the WORX, PowerSmart and DOVAMAN are push. Rear-wheel drive on the Greenworks helps uphill, and the EGO's variable 0.9 to 3.1 mph speed suits thick grass.

A wider deck cuts fewer passes, but a bigger mower is harder to store and steer. The YARDMAX has a 22 inch deck, the EGO, Greenworks, WORX and PowerSmart 21 inches, and the DOVAMAN 16 inches. Match the width to the lawn: a small, fenced yard fits a 16 inch mower, and an open half acre needs 21 inches or more.

Gas mowers need fuel stabilizer, oil changes and carburetor care, and battery mowers need cool, dry storage for the packs. Every mulching mower needs a clean deck underside, since packed clippings spoil the cut. The YARDMAX has a washout port for hosing the deck. Warranties vary: the EGO lists five years on the tool and three on batteries, and the Greenworks four years.

specDecoder.meaning: Voltage describes motor power potential and amp-hours describe stored energy. Together they set runtime, with volts times amp-hours giving watt-hours.
specDecoder.watchFor: Brochures rarely give watt-hours. The EGO's two 6.0 Ah 56V batteries hold far more than a single smaller pack.

specDecoder.meaning: Displacement in cc is the engine size. A bigger engine generally makes more torque for thick grass.
specDecoder.watchFor: Horsepower ratings are not standardized. Compare 144cc and 201cc engines by torque, as a 9.0 ft-lb figure on a 201cc engine.

specDecoder.meaning: Torque is the twisting force the blade can apply. High torque keeps the blade spinning through thick grass.
specDecoder.watchFor: Manufacturers measure it differently. The EGO's 7.0 ft-lb is a stated figure, so compare it with care.

specDecoder.meaning: These are three ways of handling clippings. Mulching recuts them, bagging collects them and side discharge throws them out.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 3-in-1 mower is not equally good at all three. Mulching quality depends on blade and deck design, not just a plug.

howToChoose.intro: The size and slope of the lawn decide the power source first.

rows: Up to three quarter acre, slopes

cards.label: Battery
cards.text: The EGO, Greenworks 60V and WORX start instantly, run quietly and need no fuel or oil. Runtime and battery cost are the limits.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: The YARDMAX and PowerSmart run until the tank is empty and handle thick grass. They are louder and need fuel, oil and carburetor care.

howToChoose.note: Choose battery for lawns up to about three quarters of an acre. Choose gas for larger, overgrown or hilly lawns.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A dedicated mulching blade, a sealed deck and enough power to keep the blade spinning. Avoid mulching wet grass or mature weed seed heads.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EGO LM2134SP-2 is the best fit, with its mulching blade and variable speed. The YARDMAX is the choice if your grass is tall and you need gas power.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a dedicated mulching blade and a long warranty, which points to the EGO. You also have slopes, which points to the Greenworks.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lawn is small and flat, where the DOVAMAN or PowerSmart is enough. You already own WORX batteries, which makes the WG752 cheaper.

maintenance.task: Scrape and rinse the deck underside
maintenance.why: Packed clippings dry into a crust that blocks airflow and spoils the cut. Disconnect power first, then clean.
A dull blade tears grass and leaves ragged clippings. A sharp blade also mulches more finely.
Dirty oil wears the engine and cuts power. Use the grade in the manual.

maintenance.task: Stabilize fuel or store batteries cool
maintenance.why: Old fuel gums carburetors, and hot or frozen batteries lose capacity. Store packs indoors at moderate temperatures.
Loose wheels change cut height, and a damaged cord is a hazard. Replace before the mowing season.

faq.q: Is a mulching mower better than bagging?
faq.a: Mulching returns nutrients to the lawn and saves emptying a bag. It works best on dry grass cut often. Bag when the grass is tall, wet or full of weed seeds.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a mulching mower?
faq.a: Corded and gas push mowers are the least expensive tier. Cordless mowers with batteries cost more, and self-propelled models with large batteries cost the most. Include batteries and fuel in the running cost.

faq.q: Do I need a special blade to mulch?
faq.a: A dedicated mulching blade works better than a plug, because it is shaped to recut clippings. The EGO includes one. A plug in a standard deck is a compromise.

faq.q: How often should I mow when mulching?
faq.a: Often enough that you remove no more than a third of the blade height. In fast growth, that can mean twice a week. Waiting too long leaves clumps.
It can if weeds have mature seed heads. Bag those cuttings, or mow before they go to seed. Mulching is fine for lawns with mostly grass.

faq.q: Is cordless strong enough for thick grass?
faq.a: Modern brushless mowers handle thick grass if the battery is large enough. Go slowly and raise the deck first. For overgrown or sloped lawns, a gas mower has more reserve.

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2134SP-2 21 in Self-Propelled Cordless Mower

specList.label: Runtime
specList.value: Up to 100 minutes with both batteries

products.description:
The EGO LM2134SP-2 is the best mulching mower here because it treats mulching as a blade system rather than a plastic plug. Its Select Cut multi-blade system uses an upper blade plus interchangeable lower blades, and the box includes a mulching blade, a high-lift bagging blade and an extended runtime blade. A mulching blade has a curved, often notched profile that keeps clippings circulating under a sealed deck so they are cut several times before dropping, which is why swapping the actual blade matters.

Torque is stated at up to 7.0 foot-pounds, which is above the 6.0 of the smaller LM2114, and the two 6.0 Ah batteries give a listed runtime of up to 100 minutes. Touch Drive self-propel lets you vary speed from 0.9 to 3.1 miles per hour with a dial, so you can slow down for thick grass where a mulching mower needs time to recut clippings. It also has eight cutting positions from 1 to 4 inches, a wider range than the Greenworks 60V and the WORX.

Ownership is easy. There is no fuel or carburetor, the brushless motor has no brushes to wear and the batteries work across other EGO tools. Scrape the underside of the deck after wet mowing, since packed clippings hurt mulching, and sharpen or replace the blade each season.
products.bestFor: Homeowners with a quarter to half acre who want a self-propelled mulching mower without gas.
pros: Interchangeable Select Cut blades include a true mulching blade
Touch Drive speed from 0.9 to 3.1 mph suits thick grass
Eight cutting heights from 1 to 4 inches cover most lawns
Two 6.0 Ah batteries are included with a five-year tool warranty
cons: Premium price among battery mowers once both batteries are counted
Heavier to turn and store than the push-only models

products.name: Greenworks 60V 21 in Self-Propelled Mower, 4-in-1

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Mulch, bag, side discharge, turbo leaf pickup

products.description:
The Greenworks 60V is aimed at bigger lawns, with a listed coverage of up to three quarters of an acre per charge from its two 4.0 Ah batteries. Coverage figures vary with grass height and terrain, so treat it as a best case. Rear-wheel drive is the right layout for slopes because it pushes the weight onto the driven wheels when you climb, which is where front-drive mowers lose traction.

The 4-in-1 system adds a turbo leaf pickup mode alongside mulching, bagging and side discharge. That extra mode is helpful in the fall when you want to collect leaves, but the mulching function is the one that matters for lawn health. Against the EGO LM2134SP-2 it lists fewer cutting-height specs and less torque information, and it carries a four-year warranty instead of five years. Against the WORX WG752 it is self-propelled and covers more ground, while the WORX is a push mower.

The Greenworks 60V platform shares batteries with a large catalog of tools, which is the main reason to buy into it. Keep the deck underside clean, store the batteries indoors in winter and charge them before use.
products.bestFor: Owners of a half to three quarters of an acre with slopes who want rear-wheel drive on a battery mower.
pros: Rear-wheel drive keeps traction when mowing uphill
Listed coverage of up to three quarters of an acre per charge
Turbo leaf pickup adds a fall cleanup mode to mulching
Four-year warranty and a battery shared with 75 plus tools
cons: Listed coverage assumes dry grass and a light cutting load
Fewer published specs than the EGO on torque and heights

products.name: WORX WG752 40V 21 in 3-in-1 Cordless Mower
products.description:
The WORX WG752 is the best-value cordless mower because it is a full 21 inch push mower with two batteries included at a lower tier than the EGO. Its AeroDeck uses a vented design that moves more air through the deck, which helps prevent clumping and fills the bag better. IntelliCut sensors raise cutting speed in thick grass and lower it in thin areas, which stretches the battery.

It powers a 40V system from two 20V 5.0 Ah PowerShare batteries, and the same batteries run more than 140 WORX tools. That is a convenience if you already own the platform, and a lock-in if you do not. It is a push mower, so on a half acre you provide the forward motion that the EGO and Greenworks supply. The mulch plug and rear discharge chute let you switch modes, but a plug is a less purpose-built mulching system than the EGO's dedicated blade.

The handle collapses for vertical storage, a real benefit in a small garage. Clean the deck after wet grass and check the plug fits snugly before mulching.
products.bestFor: Budget-minded owners of up to half an acre who want cordless mulching without self-propel.
pros: AeroDeck vented design reduces clumping and improves bagging
IntelliCut sensors raise power only when grass is thick
Two 5.0 Ah batteries are included for longer mowing
Collapsible handle allows upright storage in tight garages
cons: Push-only, so you supply the forward motion on a half acre
Mulch plug is less purpose-built than a dedicated mulching blade

products.name: YARDMAX YG2860 22 in 201cc Gas Self-Propelled Mower, CVT
products.description:
If you mow a large or hilly lawn and want gas power, the YARDMAX is the most capable machine here. A 201cc engine is a big step above the 144cc engine on the PowerSmart, and it drives a 22 inch deck, one inch wider than the 21 inch decks elsewhere. The 6-speed continuously variable transmission lets you match the drive speed to your walking pace by lever rather than by a fixed single speed.

A gas mower is a different ownership proposition from a battery mower. It requires fuel with stabilizer, regular oil changes and a blade that is kept sharp, and the engine will always be louder. In exchange it has no runtime limit, which is why it makes sense on a big or heavily overgrown lawn. Compared with the EGO, you gain unlimited mowing time and lose the quiet, the instant start and the lack of upkeep.

The washout port lets you hose the deck underside, which matters because packed clippings reduce cut quality. Change the oil each season and drain or stabilize the fuel before storage.
products.bestFor: Larger or hillier lawns where unlimited runtime matters more than quiet operation.
pros: 201cc engine gives plenty of torque for thick, tall grass
Six-speed CVT lets you set the pace without shifting gears
Automatic choke removes the priming and choking routine
Deck washout port makes cleaning the underside easy
cons: Needs fuel, oil changes and carburetor care every year
Louder than any of the battery mowers in this guide
Large 22 inch deck is bulky to store and to turn in tight yards

products.name: PowerSmart EasyGlide 21 in 144cc Gas Push Mower, 3-in-1
products.description:
The PowerSmart EasyGlide is the budget way into gas mulching. A 144cc four-stroke engine is the entry tier for a 21 inch deck, with enough power for a quarter acre of typical turf. The steel deck is durable but heavier than a composite deck, and a specialized blade helps make fine mulch, though it is a conventional blade design rather than a multi-blade system.

It is a push mower, with 10 inch rear and 7 inch front ball-bearing wheels for easier rolling, and a single-lever adjustment gives six cutting heights from 1.5 to 3.9 inches. Against the YARDMAX with a 201cc engine and a CVT drive, it has less power and no self-propel, so you do the work on slopes. Against the cordless picks it is cheaper to buy but costs more to run through fuel and upkeep.

An auto choke and primer simplify starting, which is the main complaint with small gas mowers. Check the oil before each mow, run the tank dry or add stabilizer before winter and keep the blade sharp. Mulching in tall or wet grass calls for raising the deck and taking a second pass.
products.bestFor: Homeowners with a flat quarter-acre lawn who want a low-cost gas mower that can mulch.
pros: 144cc four-stroke engine is a simple, proven design
Single-lever height adjustment offers six positions up to 3.9 inches
Large 10 inch rear wheels roll easily over uneven lawn
Auto choke and primer make cold starts less of a chore
cons: Push-only, so slopes and large lawns are hard work
Steel deck is heavier than composite or plastic alternatives
Needs regular oil changes and fuel care to stay reliable

products.name: DOVAMAN 16 in 13 Amp Corded Mulching Mower, 13.2 Gal Bag
products.description:
The DOVAMAN is the simplest mulching mower here: a 13 amp copper motor turning at up to 3500 rpm, a 16 inch deck and a cord. There is no battery to charge or replace, and no fuel to store, so it is the lowest-maintenance machine in the guide. The listing claims a 13.2 gallon bag with a fill indicator and up to 98 percent collection under typical conditions, which is a manufacturer figure for bagging rather than mulching.

The cutting heights run from 0.98 to 2.95 inches, the lowest ceiling in this guide. That matters for mulching because you should remove only about a third of the grass blade, and a 2.95 inch maximum limits you if your lawn grows tall between cuts. The 16 inch deck is also the narrowest here, so it is for small lawns. Against the cordless WORX, you give up cutting width and freedom, but you gain unlimited runtime and a lower price.

The handle folds in three steps with tool-free cam knobs and the mower stores upright. Manage the cord carefully, always mowing away from it and keeping it behind you.
products.bestFor: Small lawns near an outlet where low maintenance and storage space matter most.
pros: 13 amp corded motor needs no batteries, fuel or oil changes
Foldable handle and upright storage suit a tight garage
Large 13.2 gallon bag with a fill indicator reduces stops
Light 16 inch deck is easy to maneuver around beds
cons: Cord limits the area you can mow and needs careful handling
Maximum height of 2.95 inches is low for overgrown lawns
Narrow 16 inch deck takes more passes than the 21 inch mowers
